title: Something already happened
brief: 18:00. Endpoint security flags that a colleague clicked a bad link yesterday. You need to find out what it touched.
insight: Tom clicked a phishing link yesterday afternoon. The question is what the attacker did with the hour they had.

value.then: Forward to {{forward}}, then mark as read and delete

value.what: User visited a newly registered domain and submitted a form
details: The domain was {{fake.host}}, registered three days ago.
Sign in tokens from Tom’s session were used from {{place}} minutes later.
Check who else visited the domain, and whether any mailbox rules were added.

mail.subject: Action needed: possible account compromise (Tom Becker)
body: Yesterday a user on the finance floor submitted credentials to a newly registered domain. Please review the proxy log for who else visited it, and check your own mailbox rules and sign in activity for anything you did not create.

outcome.label: Searched the proxy log for the bad domain
outcome.what: The log shows who visited the lookalike domain. Tom and one other person did.
outcome.ideal: uses the logs to find the blast radius, not guesswork.

outcome.label: Read your own sign in activity
outcome.what: There is a sign in on your account from {{place}} yesterday, using a session token, not your authenticator.
outcome.ideal: checks their own account after a colleague is compromised.

outcome.label: Found the hidden mailbox rule
outcome.what: A rule you did not create forwards every invoice to an outside address, then deletes it so you never see it.
outcome.ideal: checks mailbox rules, where attackers hide to keep stealing invoices.

outcome.label: Raised a ticket for the incident
outcome.what: IT can reset Tom’s account and hunt for anything else the attacker left.
outcome.ideal: reports the incident so it is properly contained.

investigate.objective: Find what the attacker did, and undo it.
investigate.insight: After a compromise, attackers add an inbox rule that quietly forwards invoices out and deletes them, so the theft keeps working after the password is changed.

hint.text: Open the Terminal and grep /var/log/proxy.log for the domain in the alert. Then open Account security: read your sign in activity, and delete any mailbox rule you did not create.

outcome.label: Removed the hidden forwarding rule
outcome.what: The rule is gone. Invoices stop leaking to the outside address.
outcome.ideal: finds and removes the persistence the attacker left behind.

card.title: The back door is shut
body: You found the rule the attacker planted and deleted it. It had been quietly forwarding every invoice to an outside address, then deleting it so nobody noticed.
Changing a password does not remove a rule like this. You have to go and look for it. Now raise a ticket so IT can check Tom’s account and everything else.
card.ideal: hunts for and removes attacker persistence, not just the obvious symptom.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket so IT can reset Tom’s account and check for anything else.
